title: Suppressing Correlated Noise in Quantum Computers via Context-Aware Compiling
problem: Coherent errors that correlate among qubits in quantum processors, caused by spatial and temporal instruction configurations, degrade circuit fidelity and limit scalability for large-scale quantum computing.
motivation: Reducing correlated errors is critical for practical large-scale quantum computing, as error effects compound exponentially with circuit depth.
method: The method measures which errors happen together across multiple qubits in the quantum processor and explains why by connecting them to the physics of the superconducting hardware and how its operations work. It develops compiler strategies that reduce errors using dynamical decoupling (rapid pulses that counteract error-causing noise) and error compensation techniques. Crucially, the compiler adapts these strategies at each circuit layer by considering how qubits connect to each other, how they interfere (crosstalk), what instructions are running, and when qubits sit idle—then targets the strongest error sources in each region.
key_novelty: The core idea is a compiler strategy that adapts error suppression to match local conditions—the qubit arrangement, crosstalk (qubit interference), and what the circuit is doing—rather than applying the same suppression everywhere on the device.
contributions: Detailed experimental characterization of correlated error sources in superconducting quantum processors
Theoretical connection between noise correlations and superconducting qubit physics
Context-aware compiler strategies integrating dynamical decoupling and error compensation
18.5% layer fidelity improvement with orders of magnitude reduction in sampling overhead

metrics.other: orders of magnitude reduction in sampling overhead for multi-layer circuits

primary_theme: quantum error suppression via context-aware compilation
